findings.title: RaUF is direct radar-uncertainty prior art but is neither in the core review nor explicitly deferred
findings.evidence: RaUF is a CVPR 2026 paper that learns a physically grounded anisotropic spatial uncertainty field from radar range-azimuth-elevation intensity/Doppler input, uses LiDAR-derived occupancy ground truth, and uses Doppler consistency to reduce spurious or multipath returns. It evaluates enhanced radar point clouds on ColoRadar, RaDelft, and self-collected data, with CD/F-score, clutter point ratio, transformation-estimation, and ego-velocity endpoints. These mechanisms directly overlap the review's claims about ambiguous LiDAR supervision, radar uncertainty, multipath, Doppler, and the Teacher-Error Audit. The current retrieval artifact already identifies it as a historical coverage candidate, so it is not a new 2026-09-23..29 paper.
findings.boundary: RaUF is not evidence of occupied/free/unknown calibration, future x-y-z-t occupancy, or planning safety. The paper's reported reliability endpoints are point-cloud reconstruction/clutter and TE/EVE; the read main paper does not report occupancy ECE/Brier or independent voxel-level teacher-error truth. Its own phrase 'well-calibrated uncertainty' must not be upgraded to those stronger endpoints.
requiredCorrection: Add RaUF as core neighboring evidence because the current review already includes scene flow, neural fields, VLMs, ProOOD, and EvOcc as neighboring evidence; treating radar-specific uncertainty as out of scope would be inconsistent.

Place it in the 4D radar representation and adverse-weather/uncertainty query families, update candidateLedger/counts/query result samples/retained IDs/reference list, and use a formal CVF URL while retaining arXiv:2603.01026 as an additional link.
Update taxonomy/challenges/outlook to distinguish RaUF's anisotropic point-cloud uncertainty and LiDAR occupancy supervision from independent free/unknown/future-occupancy calibration.

If the author deliberately declines core inclusion, record an explicit deferred row with that endpoint-based reason and soften any claim that radar-specific spatial uncertainty is absent. Given the current neighboring-evidence scope, inclusion is the recommended resolution.
Recompute reviewSnapshotFingerprint and request a delta review after the correction.

findings.title: Named high-risk claims are grounded and appropriately narrowed
findings.evidence: The GPU paper independently presents a radar extension, super-resolution, histogram road-boundary extraction, and few-millisecond consumer-GPU computation; the review correctly avoids calling this automotive embedded end-to-end deployment. The DOGM paper's 'without compromising on safety' author wording has been reduced to the actual heuristic rules and explicitly denied as a formal/closed-loop safety guarantee. RadarSim's canonical project path shows code and data as coming soon; MetaOcc's repository contains README/assets/LICENSE and says code will be released soon. Elfes pages 1-2 support a multidimensional, typically 2D/3D occupancy-grid formulation rather than a 2D-only claim. Mullane's author-uploaded primary text directly supports evidential versus Bayesian radar mapping with false alarms, missed detections, and target presence/absence beliefs.

findings.title: Sless and NVRadarNet author-order conflicts are resolved using primary paper records
findings.evidence: The Sless formal PDF order is Liat Sless, Gilad Cohen, Bat El Shlomo, Shaul Oron, matching production despite Crossref's swapped middle authors. The current NVRadarNet arXiv primary page lists all eight authors in the production order; Crossref's four-author deposit is incomplete.

findings.title: The arXiv and publisher sourceAttempt status mapping is honest under the repository contract
findings.evidence: acceptedCount exactly matches references[].sourceFamily: arxiv=3 and publisher-and-venue=71. All three arXiv-owned references have primary text. Of the 71 publisher-owned references, 62 have primary text and 9 are explicitly metadata-only. The schema requires status=limited to have acceptedCount=0; therefore family-level status=success is the correct attribution status. Both rows retain discoveryOrFullTextAccessStatus=limited and notes describing the two arXiv timeouts, six arXiv 429 responses, and nine old IEEE-only full-text limitations. The rows do not imply complete recall or full-paper reading.

findings.title: HTTP success, acquisition, reading depth, and semantic support are kept separate
findings.evidence: The ledger reports 69 primary-text-checked and 9 limited references, 58 acquired full texts, and allPagesRead=false for all 78. The nine limited supports are reduced to bibliographic/topic positioning and do not carry unverified mechanisms or performance. All 279 retained byte artifacts match their recorded SHA-256; the three overwritten same-URL snapshots are preserved only as attempt metadata and explicitly point to later retained bytes.
